mainTopic: Explaining רבי אליעזר on the בת כהן who sins, and the dispute between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא over which בת כהן gets שריפה
overview: The גמרא finishes trying to explain רבי אליעזר's puzzling ruling about a בת כהן who sins: 'with her father' gets שריפה, and 'with her father-in-law' gets סקילה. One reading follows רבי ישמעאל, but רבא rejects it as inconsistent. רבא then reads it according to רבי שמעון, and רבי חנינא rejects that too. רבינא finally says רבי אליעזר follows the רבנן with the wording flipped. רב rules like רבין's explanation, which leads to a debate between רב יוסף and אביי about deciding laws that apply only in the days of משיח. Next, a ברייתא gives רבי ישמעאל's source: only an engaged בת כהן is burned, and her עדים זוממין get חנק, not שריפה. רבי עקיבא holds that a married בת כהן is also burned. He learns this from the extra ו in 'ובת', and he uses a גזרה שוה on 'אביה' to leave out an unmarried woman. The גמרא ends by showing how each תנא learns that the daughter of a blemished כהן is included, and opens a new question about רבי ישמעאל that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Reading רבי אליעזר according to רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי אליעזר according to רבי ישמעאל: 'her father' means while she is still under her father's authority (engaged), so שריפה; 'her father-in-law' means she sinned with her father-in-law himself, so סקילה; with anyone else after marriage, חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, רבי אליעזר follows רבי ישמעאל, and this is what he means: 'With her father' means while she is under her father's authority, and she gets burning. 'With her father-in-law' means she sinned with her father-in-law, and she gets stoning. And with any other man, she gets strangling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a way to make רבי אליעזר's words fit the view of רבי ישמעאל, who holds that only an engaged בת כהן gets שריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two phrases are read in two different ways. 'אביה' is not about her father as a partner. It means she is still in her father's house, so she is an ארוסה and gets שריפה. 'חמיה' is read literally: she is married and sinned with her father-in-law, which is a forbidden relation punished by סקילה. Any other man after marriage gives the normal married-woman punishment, חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth: introduces a fresh explanation
Under her father's authority, meaning still engaged and not yet married
Her father-in-law
Death by burning
Death by stoning
Death by strangling

steps.confusionAlert: 'אביה' here does NOT mean she sinned with her father. In this reading it only describes when she sinned: while still under his authority.

phrases.english: Actually, it is according to Rabbi Yishmael,
and this is what he is saying:
'With her father' means under her father's authority, by burning;
and 'with her father-in-law' means with her father-in-law himself, by stoning;
and with any other man, by strangling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier attempt on the daf to explain רבי אליעזר's statement by offering a new reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the words of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's words seemed not to fit any known opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read 'אביה' as authority and 'חמיה' literally, and it fits רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: רבא: you can't read the two phrases differently
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: why read 'father' as authority but 'father-in-law' literally? Both must be read the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the difference? Either read both of them literally, or read both of them as 'authority.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the explanation from Step 1 for being inconsistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two phrases in רבי אליעזר's statement are built the same way. There is no reason to read one as 'under the authority of' and the other as 'with the person himself.' A fair reading must treat them alike, and then the רבי ישמעאל reading falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (why treat these differently)
This one and that one: both cases
Literally, the real thing
Authority / domain

phrases.english: Rava said: What is different?
Either this one and that one are literal,
or this one and that one mean authority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading offered in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The split reading of 'אביה' and 'חמיה' in Step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Parallel phrases must be read the same way. Reading one as authority and the other literally is arbitrary.

steps.title: רבא's new reading: according to רבי שמעון, raise one level
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains רבי אליעזר according to רבי שמעון, who holds שריפה is harsher than סקילה. A married בת כהן is treated like an engaged one: each is raised one level above a regular woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Really it follows רבי שמעון, and רבי אליעזר holds that a married woman is like an engaged one. Just as we raise the engaged one by one level, from stoning to burning, so too we raise the married one by one level, from strangling to stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the first reading, רבא gives his own explanation of רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular ארוסה who sins gets סקילה, and a בת כהן ארוסה is raised to שריפה. רבי אליעזר applies the same 'one step up' rule to a נשואה: a regular married woman gets חנק, so a married בת כהן is raised to סקילה. This only works with רבי שמעון's order of severity, where שריפה is above סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: An engaged woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)
A fully married woman
One level / one step
We raise her (to a harsher punishment)
He holds / is of the opinion

steps.confusionAlert: The 'levels' depend on רבי שמעון's order, where שריפה is harsher than סקילה. That is why going up from סקילה lands on שריפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading makes the two halves of רבי אליעזר's statement one consistent rule, which fixes רבא's own complaint in Step 2.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Actually, it is according to Rabbi Shimon,
and Rabbi Eliezer holds that a married woman is like an engaged woman.

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֲרוּסָה חַד דַּרְגָּא מַסְּקִינַן לַהּ,
phrases.english: Just as for the engaged one we raise her one level,
from stoning to burning,

phrases.aramaic: אַף נְשׂוּאָה חַד דַּרְגָּא מַסְּקִינַן לַהּ,
phrases.english: so too for the married one we raise her one level,
from strangling to stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading with a new one that treats both phrases alike.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New attribution plus a guiding principle (raise one level)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר follows רבי ישמעאל with a split reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר follows רבי שמעון's order and raises both an engaged and a married בת כהן one level.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: רבי שמעון says both get burning
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא challenges רבא: רבי שמעון himself rules that both an engaged and a married בת כהן get שריפה, so how can רבי אליעזר's 'stoning for married' be following him?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא challenged it: But doesn't רבי שמעון say that in both cases she gets burning?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא attacks רבא's explanation from Step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא linked רבי אליעזר to רבי שמעון. But רבי שמעון's known ruling is that a married בת כהן also gets שריפה, not סקילה. You cannot say someone follows רבי שמעון while giving a ruling that goes against what רבי שמעון actually says.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it (attacked the explanation)
But doesn't / here (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina challenged it:
But in both this case and that case,
doesn't Rabbi Shimon say it is by burning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading from Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבי אליעזר follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון rules שריפה for both engaged and married, which contradicts סקילה for a married בת כהן.

steps.title: רבינא: Follow the רבנן and flip the wording
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that רבי אליעזר really agrees with the רבנן. We just swap the two punishments in his statement: 'her father' (engaged) gets סקילה, and 'her father-in-law' (married) gets שריפה. He said 'her father' only because that is the wording people were used to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבינא says: Really, רבי אליעזר follows the רבנן. Just flip his words: 'with her father' means stoning, and 'with her father-in-law' means burning. The reason he used the phrase 'her father' is just that he was following a common way of speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: After רבא's explanation fell apart, רבינא gives a brand-new answer. רבי אליעזר agrees with the רבנן, and we simply reverse the two punishments in his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier attempts tried to fit רבי אליעזר's wording as it stands, using רבי ישמעאל or רבי שמעון. רבינא instead keeps the mainstream view of the רבנן: engaged gets סקילה and married gets שריפה. He fixes the problem by flipping the text. The odd phrase 'her father' (meaning 'while engaged') is explained as just a familiar way of talking, taken from the wording of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; signals going back to a simpler position
Reverse it; swap the two parts of the statement
A habit of speech; a familiar way of phrasing something
He used / took up (a wording)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'her father' here means she sinned with her father. It is just a way of saying 'while she is still under her father's authority,' meaning engaged.

phrases.english: Rather, Ravina said:
Actually, it follows the Rabbis,
and reverse the wording:
with her father — by stoning,
and with her father-in-law — by burning.
And the fact that he says 'with her father' —
he was merely following a common way of speaking.
phrases.notes: He means the phrase 'her father' comes from the wording of the פסוק, so it was a natural way to say 'engaged.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבִינָא: לְעוֹלָם כְּרַבָּנַן, וְאֵיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's explanation, which was rejected by רבי חנינא in step 4, with a new reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual reversal: the statement is read in the opposite order, and the odd wording is explained as a habit of speech.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רבי אליעזר's words must be read exactly in their order, which forced us to find a תנא who gives married women סקילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר follows the רבנן: engaged gets סקילה and married gets שריפה. His words are simply flipped, and 'her father' is just a familiar way of saying 'engaged.'

steps.title: רב rules like the explanation רבין sent
steps.stepSummary: רב, through a chain of teachers, rules that the הלכה follows the explanation רבין sent in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה, in the name of רב: The הלכה follows what רבין sent in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings a ruling: the הלכה follows the explanation רבין sent from ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא was only trying to explain רבי אליעזר's words. Here רב decides between the explanations and says which one is the הלכה. This sets up רב יוסף's objection in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The binding law; the ruling we follow
Sent (a teaching sent by message from ארץ ישראל)
In the name of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
The halacha follows what Ravin sent
phrases.notes: This points back to an explanation רבין sent from ארץ ישראל, quoted earlier in the סוגיא.

phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ, אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּדִשְׁלַח רָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רבי אליעזר's words to giving a ruling on which explanation is the הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows the explanation רבין sent in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Why rule on a law for the days of משיח?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects: deciding this is like ruling on a law for the time of משיח, since today courts don't judge cases of death penalties.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Are we deciding הלכה for the days of משיח?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רב's ruling. He asks why we bother deciding a law that won't be used until משיח comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Death penalties like סקילה and שריפה are only carried out by a court when the בית המקדש stands. So right now this law has no practical use, and רב יוסף questions the point of deciding it.

keyTerms.meaning: A ruling of law (Aramaic form of הֲלָכָה)
For the time of משיח

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
A halacha for the days of Mashiach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the usefulness of רב's ruling in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the הלכה follows רבין's explanation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling is meant for practice. This law cannot be practiced until the days of משיח, so why decide it now?

steps.title: אביי: We learn such laws for the reward of learning
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back: if that were true, we shouldn't learn the laws of slaughtering קרבנות either. We learn them anyway because learning Torah brings reward, and the same is true here.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, we shouldn't learn the laws of slaughtering קרבנות, since that is also a law for the days of משיח! Rather, we learn and get reward for it. Here too, we learn and get reward.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רב יוסף's objection. He shows that we learn plenty of laws that aren't practical today, like the laws of קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי uses a comparison: the laws of שחיטת קדשים also only apply when the בית המקדש stands, yet we learn them. The reason is that learning Torah is a מצוה with its own reward. So deciding a law that is not practical today is still worthwhile.

keyTerms.meaning: If that is so (introduces a strange result of the other side's logic)
Slaughtering of holy offerings (the laws of קרבנות)
Learn and receive reward; Torah learning is rewarded even when it isn't practical

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known principle: learning Torah has value in itself, even for laws that cannot be practiced today.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
If that is so,
should we not learn the slaughtering of holy offerings?
It is a halacha for the days of Mashiach!
Rather, learn and receive reward.
Here too, learn and receive reward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, שְׁחִיטַת קֳדָשִׁים לָא לִיתְנֵי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's objection from step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that a law which is not practical today is not worth deciding.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If it were true, we would also have to stop learning the laws of קרבנות. Yet we learn them, because Torah learning brings reward.

steps.title: רב יוסף clarifies: This discussion has no halacha to decide
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains what he really meant: he wasn't against learning it. His point was that this discussion is only about how to read רבי אליעזר's words, so there is nothing to rule on as הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what I meant: Why do we need a ruling of הלכה here? Does anyone say 'הלכה' about a discussion that only explains the wording of a teaching?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי by explaining his real point. Ruling on a 'הלכה' here doesn't make sense, because the explanations don't disagree on the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף agrees that we learn laws for the time of משיח. His real problem is different: all the opinions here are just ways of explaining רבי אליעזר's wording. Since they don't argue about what the law actually is, saying 'the הלכה follows this one' is out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I meant to say
Why do I need it?
The discussion explaining a teaching (how to read its words)

steps.whatToRemember: רבינא reads רבי אליעזר like the רבנן with the wording flipped. רב rules like רבין's explanation, and רב יוסף's final point is that this is only a debate about wording, not a real difference in law.

phrases.english: This is what I meant to say:
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is speaking here, explaining his earlier question.

phrases.english: Why do I need a halacha?
Does one state a halacha about a discussion that explains a teaching?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אביי's rejection in step 8 by restating רב יוסף's objection in a sharper form.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling in step 6 that the הלכה follows רבין's explanation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The explanations only argue about how to read רבי אליעזר's words, not about the actual law. So stating a 'הלכה' between them adds nothing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement over רבי אליעזר's statement is about wording only. That is why a ruling of הלכה here seems unnecessary.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי ישמעאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי ישמעאל's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the source for רבי ישמעאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי ישמעאל gets his view. This sets up the next move, where a ברייתא will be brought as the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל holds that only an engaged בת כהן who sins is punished with שריפה. A married בת כהן gets the regular punishment for adultery. The גמרא now wants the source for this split.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who limits the שריפה of a בת כהן to an engaged woman
What? Here it means 'what is the source for'

phrases.english: What is [the source of] Rabbi Yishmael?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting aside the discussion of how to read רבי אליעזר's words, the גמרא turns to the source for רבי ישמעאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי ישמעאל's view that שריפה applies only to an engaged בת כהן.

steps.title: The verse speaks of an engaged young woman
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the פסוק of a בת כהן who sins speaks about a נערה who is an ארוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And the daughter of a כהן, when she profanes herself by sinning.' The פסוק is speaking about a young woman who is engaged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source. The ברייתא says the פסוק about a בת כהן being burned speaks only about an engaged young woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line states the rule but does not yet prove it. The ברייתא will now question its own claim and then bring a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Profanes herself by sinning (adultery)
A young woman, just past the age of maturity
Engaged with קידושין, but not yet fully married

phrases.english: As it is taught: "And the daughter of [a man who is] a priest
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:9. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, so it matches the פסוק exactly.

phrases.english: when she profanes herself by playing the harlot" —
the verse is speaking of a young woman who is betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ישמעאל's view that שריפה applies only to an engaged בת כהן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 21:9 as speaking of a נערה המאורסה

steps.title: Maybe the verse includes a married woman too
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks itself: why only an engaged woman? Maybe a married בת כהן is also burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it means a young engaged woman. Or maybe it means even a married woman?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own claim. It asks why we should limit the פסוק to an engaged woman, since the פסוק does not say so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק just says 'בת כהן' with no limit. So the simple reading could include a married woman too. This question sets up the proof that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: You say (a ברייתא formula that tests its own claim)
Or perhaps it is really
A fully married woman (after חופה)

phrases.english: Do you say it is a young woman who is betrothed,
or is it really even a married woman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the limit stated in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק of בת כהן should be limited to an ארוסה and not include a נשואה.

steps.title: Proof by comparing to the daughter of a non-priest
steps.stepSummary: All adulterers fall under the general פסוק. The Torah took out the engaged בת ישראל for סקילה and the בת כהן for שריפה. Just as the בת ישראל exception is only an ארוסה, so is the בת כהן exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'A man who commits adultery with his neighbor's wife, the adulterer and the adulteress shall be put to death.' Everyone was included in 'the adulterer and the adulteress.' Then the Torah took out the בת ישראל for סקילה and the בת כהן for שריפה. When the Torah took out the בת ישראל for סקילה, it meant an engaged woman, not a married one. So too, when it took out the בת כהן for שריפה, it means an engaged woman, not a married one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. There is a general rule for all adulterers, and two exceptions. The exceptions are compared so they work the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every adulteress starts under the general פסוק and its regular punishment. The Torah made two exceptions: the בת ישראל gets סקילה, and the בת כהן gets שריפה. The בת ישראל exception is clearly only for an ארוסה, so the בת כהן exception is read the same way. A married בת כהן stays under the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces the proof verse)
The adulterer and the adulteress
Everyone was included in the general rule
The פסוק took out (made an exception)
Death by stoning / death by burning

steps.whatToRemember: A married בת כהן stays under the general rule for adulterers. Only the engaged בת כהן is taken out for שריפה, just as only the engaged בת ישראל is taken out for סקילה.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"A man who commits adultery with his neighbor's wife,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:10

phrases.english: the adulterer and the adulteress shall be put to death."
All were included in
"the adulterer and the adulteress."
phrases.notes: This general פסוק carries the regular death for adultery, which is חנק (strangling).

phrases.english: The verse took out the daughter of a non-priest for stoning
and the daughter of a priest for burning.
Just as when the verse took out
the daughter of a non-priest for stoning —
it was a betrothed woman and not a married one,
so too, when the verse took out
the daughter of a priest for burning —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 with a proof from a פסוק and a comparison.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two exceptions to the general adultery rule are compared. Since the בת ישראל exception is only for an ארוסה, the בת כהן exception is also only for an ארוסה.

steps.title: Her false witnesses and her partner fall under 'as he plotted'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the זוממין of a בת כהן and her בועל are included in 'ועשיתם לו כאשר זמם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her plotting witnesses and the man who sinned with her are included in 'And you shall do to him as he plotted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a new rule about the false witnesses (זוממין) against a בת כהן and about her partner in the sin. The wording is puzzling, and the גמרא will question it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally עדים זוממין receive the same punishment they tried to bring on the person they accused. The ברייתא connects both the זוממין and the בועל to that פסוק. It is not yet clear how this works.

keyTerms.meaning: Her עדים זוממין: witnesses proven to have lied to get her punished
The man who sinned with her
Do to him what he plotted (to do to his brother), the punishment for עדים זוממין

phrases.english: Her conspiring witnesses and her paramour
are included in "And you shall do to him
as he conspired, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 19:19

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹמְמֶיהָ וּבוֹעֲלָהּ בִּכְלַל וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר זָמַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new rule about her זוממין and her בועל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זוממין of a בת כהן and her בועל are linked to the rule of 'כאשר זמם'.

steps.title: How does 'as he plotted' apply to her partner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'כאשר זמם' has to do with the בועל, who plotted nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her partner — what 'as he plotted' is there with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's wording. The partner in the sin did not lie or plot against anyone, so the פסוק about plotting witnesses does not fit him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כאשר זמם' only applies to witnesses who lied to get someone punished. The בועל really sinned and did not testify. So putting him under 'כאשר זמם' makes no sense as written.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there? (meaning: how does this apply at all?)

phrases.english: Her paramour — what "as he conspired" is there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that the בועל is included in 'כאשר זמם'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'כאשר זמם' applies only to lying witnesses. The בועל did not plot or testify, so the פסוק cannot apply to him.

steps.title: Her false witnesses get her partner's death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: her זוממין are included in the death of her בועל. They get חנק, not שריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: her plotting witnesses are included in the death of her partner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא. The זוממין of a בת כהן are not burned as she would have been. They receive the death of her partner instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not mean that the בועל is under 'כאשר זמם'. It means the זוממין receive the בועל's punishment, which is חנק. They are not burned, even though they plotted to have her burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a corrected reading)
The death penalty of her partner (חנק)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the זוממין are burned because they plotted to have her burned. They get the בועל's death (חנק), not hers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a unique outcome within the category of עדים זוממין. They are still זוממין, but here they do not receive exactly the death they plotted for her.
steps.whatToRemember: The זוממין of a בת כהן get the death of her partner (חנק), not her death (שריפה).

phrases.english: Rather: her conspiring witnesses
are included in the death of her paramour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that both the זוממין and the בועל fall under 'כאשר זמם'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means that the זוממין receive the בועל's death (חנק) rather than her שריפה.

steps.title: The verse behind the rule: 'to his brother' and not 'to his sister'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives its source: the פסוק says the plotting witnesses are punished for what they planned 'to his brother', not 'to his sister'. So they get the בועל's death, חנק, and not her שריפה. This is רבי ישמעאל's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is because the פסוק says: 'And you shall do to him as he plotted to do to his brother', and not to his sister. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its point from step 16 by quoting the פסוק that proves the עדים זוממין get the man's punishment and not the woman's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses wanted to have both the בת כהן burned and the man choked. The פסוק says 'to his brother', so we only copy the punishment they planned for the man (חנק). The punishment they planned for the woman (שריפה) is not given to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses proven to have lied, who get the punishment they tried to cause
To his brother: the man who was accused
To his sister: here, the woman who was accused
Death by choking, the punishment of the בועל

steps.confusionAlert: The witnesses are not let off. They still get the death penalty; it is just חנק (the man's punishment) and not שריפה (her punishment).

phrases.english: Because it is stated:
"And you shall do to him as he plotted
phrases.notes: דברים 19:19

phrases.english: to do to his brother,"
and not to his sister.
phrases.notes: So the witnesses get what they planned for the man, not what they planned for the woman.

phrases.english: These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר זָמַם לַעֲשׂוֹת לְאָחִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the reread rule of step 16 and closes רבי ישמעאל's ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עדים זוממין of a בת כהן get חנק, like her בועל, because the פסוק says 'לאחיו' and not 'לאחותו'.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: both engaged and married get burning
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי ישמעאל. He holds that a בת כהן who sins, whether she is an ארוסה or a נשואה, gets שריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: both an engaged woman and a married woman are singled out for burning.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the second opinion comes in. רבי עקיבא says that the married בת כהן also gets שריפה, not only the engaged one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 13, רבי ישמעאל limited שריפה to an engaged בת כהן. רבי עקיבא widens the rule to include a married בת כהן too. The next steps show how he sets limits on his rule and where he learns it from.

keyTerms.meaning: An engaged woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)
A fully married woman
Death by burning
Was taken out, singled out from the general rule

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says:
Both an engaged woman and a married woman
were singled out for burning.
phrases.notes: He means a בת כהן, taken out of the general adultery rule and given burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing opinion to רבי ישמעאל's view from steps 12-13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בת כהן who commits adultery, whether engaged or married, gets שריפה.

steps.title: Maybe even an unmarried girl?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי עקיבא made the rule wider, the ברייתא asks if it goes all the way to a בת כהן who is not married or engaged at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that even an unmarried woman is burned?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible question to set up the next step: does רבי עקיבא's rule cover even a single, unmarried בת כהן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the rule is not limited to an ארוסה, you might think any act of זנות by a בת כהן brings שריפה. This question sets the stage for the source that limits it.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (introduces a wrong idea that will be rejected)
Even
An unmarried woman, not tied to any husband

phrases.english: One might think, even an unmarried woman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far רבי עקיבא's wider rule goes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does שריפה apply even to a בת כהן who has no husband at all?

steps.title: The word 'her father' shows she must have a husband
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אביה' appears in the פסוק about the בת כהן and in the פסוק about the engaged girl. Through a גזרה שוה, just as there she is tied to a husband, so too here. So a פנויה is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says here 'her father', and it says there 'her father'. Just as there it is זנות while tied to a husband, so too here it is זנות while tied to a husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question: an unmarried בת כהן is not burned, and it proves this by comparing two פסוקים that share the word 'אביה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אביה' links the בת כהן פסוק to the פסוק of the engaged girl who sinned. That girl was tied to a husband, so the בת כהן who gets שריפה must also be tied to a husband. This keeps the פנויה out, but still lets in both ארוסה and נשואה.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one פסוק from another because they share the same word
Her father: the shared word that links the two פסוקים
Forbidden relations
A bond to a husband (being engaged or married)
There (the other פסוק) / here (this פסוק)

phrases.english: It is stated here: "her father,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:9, the פסוק about the בת כהן.

phrases.english: and it is stated there: "her father."
phrases.notes: דברים 22:21, the engaged girl who sinned.

phrases.english: Just as there it is forbidden relations
while bound to a husband,
so too here it is forbidden relations
while bound to a husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן אָבִיהָ וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן אָבִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Through a גזרה שוה on 'אביה', only a בת כהן with a bond to a husband gets שריפה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: then copy the whole case, an engaged נערה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל turns רבי עקיבא's own comparison against him. If you learn from the engaged girl, then copy all her details: she must be a נערה who is engaged, not married.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said to him: If so, just as there it is a young girl who is engaged, so too here it is a young girl who is engaged.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל challenges רבי עקיבא, using the same גזרה שוה to prove his own view that only an engaged בת כהן is burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case 'there' is not just any woman with a husband. It is a נערה who is engaged. If the comparison is real, it should limit the בת כהן to that same case, which leaves out the married woman.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if you use this comparison)
A young girl, in the first months after becoming an adult
Just as ... so too (the form of a comparison)

phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל said to him:
If so, just as there
it is a young girl and she is engaged,
so too here, a young girl and she is engaged.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: אִי, מָה לְהַלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the גזרה שוה of step 20 and רבי עקיבא's ruling in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling that a married בת כהן is also burned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the 'אביה' comparison is real, it should copy every detail of the engaged girl, so only an engaged נערה gets שריפה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: I learn it from the extra ו in 'ובת'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that he learns the married woman from the extra letter ו: the פסוק says 'ובת' instead of just 'בת'. The extra letter adds the married בת כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: ישמעאל my brother, I learn from 'בת' versus 'ובת'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers רבי ישמעאל's challenge by showing he has a separate source that adds the married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא agrees the גזרה שוה alone would limit her to an engaged נערה. But the extra ו in 'ובת איש כהן' adds more cases, so the married woman is included. The גזרה שוה is only used to keep out the פנויה.

keyTerms.meaning: ישמעאל my brother: a friendly way of addressing a fellow sage
And the daughter: the word with the extra ו
I learn out, I explain the פסוק
An addition: an extra word or letter that includes more cases

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל: only an engaged בת כהן gets שריפה, and her עדים זוממין get חנק. רבי עקיבא: both an engaged and a married בת כהן get שריפה (from the extra ו in 'ובת'), but not a פנויה (from the גזרה שוה on 'אביה').

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא said to him:
ישמעאל, my brother,
I learn from "daughter" versus "and the daughter."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָחִי, בַּת וּבַת אֲנִי דּוֹרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ישמעאל's challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a separate source (an extra letter) for the part of the rule that was challenged.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's whole rule depended on the 'אביה' comparison, which would limit it to an engaged נערה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The married woman is included through the extra ו in 'ובת'. The comparison is only used to keep out the פנויה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל says the extra letter cannot pick and choose
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל argues that if the ו is broad enough to add a נשואה, it should also add a פנויה. If it is not broad enough for the פנויה, it should not add the נשואה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Just because you expound 'בת' versus 'ובת', we should send this married woman to burning? If the extra letter includes the married woman, it should include the unmarried woman too. And if it excludes the unmarried woman, it should exclude the married woman too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל pushes back against רבי עקיבא's answer from Step 22. He says one extra letter cannot include one woman and leave out another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra ו is a general 'add more' signal. Nothing in it tells you to stop at the married woman. So either it adds everyone, including the פנויה, or it adds no one, and the married woman should not get שריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounds; learns a law from the wording of a פסוק
Burning, the death penalty for a בת כהן who sins
To include
To exclude
An unmarried woman, neither engaged nor married

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי ישמעאל speaking to רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: And just because you expound
'daughter' versus 'and daughter'
we should take this one out to be burned?
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the married בת כהן.

phrases.english: If it means to include the married woman,
then include the unmarried woman too;
and if it means to exclude the unmarried woman,
then exclude the married woman too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאַתָּה דּוֹרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the extra-ו answer that רבי עקיבא gave in Step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's use of the ו in 'ובת' to include the נשואה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An extra letter is an all-or-nothing signal. It cannot include the נשואה and still leave out the פנויה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא uses two sources working together
steps.stepSummary: For רבי עקיבא, the גזירה שוה removes the פנויה, and the extra ו adds the נשואה. Each source does its own job.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how would רבי עקיבא answer? The גזירה שוה works to exclude the unmarried woman, and 'בת / ובת' works to include the married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי עקיבא. He never relied on the ו alone. He combines it with the גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's attack assumed the ו was the only source. But the גזירה שוה of 'אביה' already ties the case to a woman connected to a husband, so the פנויה is out. Inside that limit, the ו stretches the case from an ארוסה to a נשואה.

keyTerms.meaning: It works, it serves a purpose
To exclude, to narrow down
To include, to widen
Learning one case from another through a word that appears in both

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא uses two tools. The גזירה שוה sets the outer edge, so no פנויה. The ו widens the case inside that edge, so the נשואה is included.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva?
The verbal analogy works
to exclude the unmarried woman,
and 'daughter / and daughter' works
to include the married woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי עקיבא against the attack in Step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining two sources, each with its own job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא relies on the ו alone, so it must include everyone or no one
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה excludes the פנויה, and the ו includes the נשואה

steps.title: Why רבי ישמעאל attacked anyway
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל thought that once רבי עקיבא brought up the ו, he had given up on the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל thought: Since רבי עקיבא told him 'בת / ובת', we can learn from this that he took back the גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי ישמעאל made his attack, even though רבי עקיבא really had two sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל understood the switch to the ו as dropping the גזירה שוה. Without the גזירה שוה, the ו stands alone, and then his all-or-nothing attack would work. In fact, רבי עקיבא kept both sources.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought, he understood
Learn from this
He retracted, he took it back

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael thought:
since he said to him 'daughter / and daughter,'
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי עקיבא, answering in Step 22.

phrases.english: learn from this
that he took back the verbal analogy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי ישמעאל made the attack in Step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the attack came from a misunderstanding
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא dropped the גזירה שוה and relied only on the ו
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא kept the גזירה שוה, so the attack does not hit him

steps.title: What does רבי ישמעאל learn from the extra letter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי ישמעאל does with the extra ו in 'ובת', since he does not use it for the married woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל, what does he learn from this 'בת / ובת'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. If רבי ישמעאל rejects רבי עקיבא's reading, what is the extra ו there for in his view? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק's extra letter is assumed to teach something. Since רבי ישמעאל does not use it to include the נשואה, he must use it for some other law.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael,
this 'daughter / and daughter',
what does he learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, הַאי ״בַּת״ ״וּבַת״ מַאי דָּרֵישׁ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רבי עקיבא to explaining רבי ישמעאל's own reading of the פסוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What law רבי ישמעאל learns from the extra ו in 'ובת'

steps.title: The daughter of a blemished כהן is included
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל uses the ו to teach that the daughter of a כהן with a מום also gets שריפה, just like the daughter of a כהן without one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what the father of שמואל בר אבין taught: Since we find that the Torah treats male כהנים differently, unblemished ones versus blemished ones, might we also treat their daughters differently? The פסוק teaches: 'בת / ובת'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל uses the ו for a different lesson, taught in a ברייתא. Daughters of blemished כהנים are included in the law of שריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן with a מום may not do the עבודה. So you might think his daughter is not counted as a full בת כהן for this law. The extra ו teaches that she is still included and gets שריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it, he uses it for
Unblemished, without a מום
Blemished people, who have a מום
Might you think?
The פסוק teaches

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים use the ו in 'ובת'. רבי עקיבא uses it to include the married בת כהן. רבי ישמעאל uses it to include the daughter of a blemished כהן.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the argument is not about whether the ו teaches something. Both agree it does. They argue only about what it adds.

phrases.english: He needs it
for what the father of Shmuel bar Avin taught:
Since we find that the verse made a difference among males
phrases.notes: He means male כהנים: only unblemished ones may do the עבודה.

phrases.english: between unblemished ones and blemished ones,
might we make a difference among their daughters?
The verse teaches: 'daughter / and daughter.'

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's source for the daughter of a כהן with a מום
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns that a כהן בעל מום is still holy from the פסוק 'הם מקריבם והיו קדש', so his daughter is treated like any בת כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא learns it from the verse 'they offer them, and they shall be holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quietly asks where רבי עקיבא gets the בעל מום rule, since he already used the extra ו for the married woman. It answers that he learns it from a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא used up the ו on the נשואה, so he needs another source to include the daughter of a blemished כהן. The words 'והיו קדש' teach that every כהן stays holy, even one who cannot bring קרבנות because of a מום. So there is no difference between his daughter and the daughter of a כהן without a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: They offer them. A phrase from ויקרא 21:6 about the כהנים bringing קרבנות.
And they shall be holy. The words that show every כהן is holy, even one with a מום.
It comes out from. Used to say 'he learns it from this source.'

phrases.english: And רבי עקיבא
phrases.notes: The question is left unspoken: since he used the ו for the married woman, where does he learn the בעל מום case?

phrases.english: from 'they offer them
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:6

phrases.english: and they shall be holy': he derives it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 27 gives רבי ישמעאל's use of the ו, this step gives רבי עקיבא's separate source for the same rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא learns the daughter of a כהן בעל מום from 'הם מקריבם והיו קדש', which shows that a blemished כהן is still holy.

steps.title: Why רבי ישמעאל needs the ו and not just that פסוק
steps.stepSummary: From 'והיו קדש' alone, one might think only the כהנים themselves stay holy, not their daughters. So רבי ישמעאל needs the ו in 'ובת' to include the daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל? If we only had that verse, I would have said: that applies only to the כהנים themselves, but not to their daughters. So the ו teaches us that it applies to the daughters too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל does not just use רבי עקיבא's פסוק. It answers that the פסוק talks only about the כהנים themselves, so the ו is needed to cover their daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'והיו קדש' is said about the כהנים, so it proves that a כהן with a מום keeps his holiness. It does not clearly reach his daughter. רבי ישמעאל therefore uses the ו in 'ובת' to teach that the daughter of a blemished כהן also gets שריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said. What we might have mistakenly thought without this source.
These words apply. This limits a rule to a certain case.
Their daughters.
It teaches us. The source is needed to show us something new.

phrases.english: And רבי ישמעאל?

this applies to them themselves,

phrases.english: but not to their daughters.
So it teaches us.
phrases.notes: The 'it' is the extra ו in 'ובת', which includes the daughters.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, אִי מֵהַהִיא הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 28 gave רבי עקיבא's source. This step explains why רבי ישמעאל cannot rely on that source alone.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'והיו קדש' would only include the blemished כהנים themselves, not their daughters. So the ו is needed for the daughters.
steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree that the daughter of a כהן בעל מום gets שריפה. רבי עקיבא learns it from 'והיו קדש'. רבי ישמעאל says that פסוק only covers the כהנים themselves, so he learns the daughters from the ו in 'ובת'.

steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words appear here, so we do not yet know what is being asked. These words show that the גמרא is turning to look more closely at רבי ישמעאל's position.
